purpose: Test whether S2 attains the same per-trace receiver utility as eager dual execution while running the conventional branch only after a natural NeuralRx CRC/payload failure and reclaiming the remaining same-GPU MPS slack for AI work.

selection_source.confirm18_transition: At -8.5 dB, conventional=180/500, NeuralRx=489/500, union=491/500, with 2 conventional-only successes.
selection_source.smoke19b: On 100 fixed-seed traces after channel-path warmup, NRx-only=94, eager-dual=95, and S2=95 with zero deadline misses and zero duplicate commits.

radio.input: Aerial PdschTx-generated valid 273-PRB PUSCH; the identical immutable noisy slot is supplied to both receivers
radio.channel: independent block-Rayleigh coefficient per RX antenna plus complex AWGN
radio.paired_trace_rule: Within each round, every policy uses the same payload seed and channel seed for each release.

fault_model.failure_signal: the measured receiver CRC and payload equality on the natural noisy channel

background.kind: separate MPS NeuralRx CUDA Graph client

policies.eager_dual: execute both actual receiver branches on every release and commit NeuralRx when valid, otherwise conventional
policies.s2_reserved: reserve NeuralRx and a delayed conventional recovery interval atomically; execute conventional only when NeuralRx cannot commit; allow exactly one branch to commit

execution_order: Forward policy order on odd rounds and reverse order on even rounds.
interpretation_limit: The timing claims are empirical for the declared A100/MPS configuration and workload bounds; they are not an unconditional hardware isolation proof.
